title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
summary: Given an array of points with integer coordinates on a 2D-plane, calculate the minimum cost to connect all points using the Manhattan distance.
statement: Given an array of points with integer coordinates on a 2D-plane, calculate the minimum cost to connect all points using the Manhattan distance. The cost to connect two points is the sum of the absolute differences in their x and y coordinates. Ensure there is exactly one path between any two points.
constraints: Connect all points with Manhattan-distance edges so exactly one path exists between every pair.
Return the minimum total edge cost.
hints: Use Prim’s algorithm starting from any point.
Maintain each unconnected point’s cheapest Manhattan edge to the connected set.
Repeatedly add the cheapest such point and relax distances from it.
The cut property proves every selected cheapest crossing edge belongs to some minimum spanning tree.
editorial: The cut property proves every selected cheapest crossing edge belongs to some minimum spanning tree.
